questions.text: What is the register map of the test shell (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: The map in registers.map: PKT_BYTE 0x00, TICK 0x04, STATUS 0x08, REPLY_LEN 0x0C, REPLY_IDX 0x10, REPLY_WORD 0x14, TELEM_LEN 0x18, TELEM_IDX 0x1C, TELEM_WORD 0x20, TAKE 0x24, all 32 bits.
questions.reason: The request names shell registers but gives no offsets, so the map is proposed, not known.
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)
questions.evidence: IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag

questions.text: How does the host give the last-byte flag?
questions.reason: The request says a flag on the last byte but not how the shell carries it.
questions.answer: Bit 8 of a write to register IN (offset 0x00), with the packet byte in bits [7:0]. The spec names this register IN, not PKT_BYTE, so the proposed default's name does not match the spec.

questions.text: Does a refused telemetry start change the period?
questions.answer: No. A refused packet changes no telemetry state, and the period belongs to the telemetry pacer, so a refused TLM_START leaves the period unchanged.
questions.evidence: a refused packet changes no register, sequence or telemetry state

questions.text: What are the values of TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?
questions.reason: They are supplied by the shell and not stated.
questions.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000. BUILD_STAMP is not specified, so no value can be given for it. The proposed default of 1000000 for TIMEOUT_CYCLES does not match the specification.

questions.text: Is the first telemetry frame due on the period-th tick after start?
questions.reason: The request says start restarts the count and a frame falls due every period-th tick.
questions.answer: Yes. Telemetry frames fall due every period-th tick, and TLM_START restarts the count.
questions.evidence: telemetry frames fall due every period-th tick, one is held at most, overruns are dropped, stop forgets a held frame
